title: bug: launcher pre-flight /health probes skip the foreign-project check for a named MOE_DAEMON_HOST: moe-agent.sh sends the name and gets 403, moe-agent.ps1 only ever probes 127.0.0.1
description:
post-switch: lane paths. Held in BACKLOG on the governor's ruling (msg-05a7ca6e, 2026-11-02 17:45Z): promote it after the worktree switch, when lane rows run in parallel worktrees.

Files: scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs. All three are lane paths. At filing, 25 open rows declared one or both launchers (scan of affectedFiles + modifiedFiles, 17:50Z). The nearest overlap is WORKING task-3def0804. It declares all three files and edits the same two probes: comparable() inside probe_daemon_health, and Get-MoeComparableProjectPath. So this row dependsOn it. It also dependsOn task-86d66093, the proxy half of this bug, so it mirrors the rule that lands there.

Origin: this is the launcher half of task-86d66093 (moe-proxy probeDaemonIdentity) and of task-f0abb6d6, which fixed the daemon CLI's own probe with healthProbeAddress in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts. The daemon's /health Host guard is isAllowedHealthHost in packages/moe-daemon/src/server/healthHost.ts (task-80930ce6). It admits only localhost, 127.x, ::1 and the address the connection arrived on, so any other DNS name in Host gets 403, by design.

Repro, 2026-11-02 ~17:53Z. I extracted the probe_daemon_health function verbatim from scripts/moe-agent.sh and ran it against a fake /health on 127.0.1.1 that applies the daemon's real isAllowedHealthHost. The machine name resolves to 127.0.1.1 in /etc/hosts.
- By IP (127.0.1.1): another project gives rc 3 (foreign, refused), and this project gives rc 0.
- By the machine name: both projects give rc 1. urllib gets HTTPError 403, and the probe exits 1 for any code but 503. curl by name also gets 403.

Effects in scripts/moe-agent.sh:
1. Live-PID branch (PROBE_HOST is MOE_DAEMON_HOST, else 127.0.0.1): rc 1 is not 3, so RUNNING=true. The seat adopts another project's daemon with no MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT, which turns off the stale-daemon.json guard from task-e7f4026a for every named host.
2. Windows-daemon branch (candidates in order: MOE_DAEMON_HOST, 127.0.0.1, the WSL gateway): the named candidate always fails, so a foreign daemon at that name is never refused. The loop falls through. It then either exports the first later candidate that answers as MOE_DAEMON_HOST, replacing the operator's name, or exits 1 as not reachable from here, though the daemon answers at that name.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (code read, not run): Get-MoeDaemonIdentity always dials 127.0.0.1 and sends Host 127.0.0.1:PORT, and its only caller passes no host. So it never sees the 403, but it never checks MOE_DAEMON_HOST either. A daemon that does not listen on 127.0.0.1 reads as unknown and is adopted. Its refusal line also hard-codes 127.0.0.1.

Fix direction, mirroring healthProbeAddress and task-86d66093:
- Resolve a host that is neither an IP literal nor localhost (any case) once, take the first address in OS order, and request /health from that IP literal. The Host is then an IP literal the guard admits, bracketed for IPv6.
- IP literals and localhost keep today's request byte for byte.
- ps1 probes MOE_DAEMON_HOST when set, else 127.0.0.1, under the same rule, and its refusal names the probed host. The three refusal sentences stay byte-identical to sh.
- The sh candidate loop still exports the candidate as given, never the resolved IP.

Error handling: a failed or hung lookup counts as unreachable (sh rc 1, ps1 unknown) inside the existing 3 s bound. Neither launcher may hang or throw while resolving.

Test hint: the launchers have no resolver hook. A real name path needs a name that resolves locally. os.hostname() works if the fake listens on exactly the address it resolves to, with no test-only switch in the launchers. Skip the row, with a reason, when the name does not resolve to a local address.

Out of scope: the Host guard itself (healthHost.ts stays byte-identical) and the proxy (task-86d66093). The JetBrains and VS Code probes were not checked.
definitionOfDone: scripts/moe-agent.sh probe_daemon_health resolves a host that is neither an IP literal nor localhost (any case) once, takes the first address in OS order, and requests /health from that IP literal. The Host it sends is then an IP literal, bracketed for IPv6, that isAllowedHealthHost admits. IP-literal and localhost hosts send today's request unchanged. Both call sites, the live-PID identity check and the Windows-daemon candidate loop, get the fix through the function, and the loop still exports the candidate as given.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1's pre-flight identity probe dials MOE_DAEMON_HOST when it is set, else 127.0.0.1, under the same resolve rule. The MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT refusal names the probed host and port. The three refusal sentences stay byte-identical to moe-agent.sh, and the test 'identity: both launchers carry the same MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT refusal' passes.

Error handling: on both launchers, a failed lookup and a lookup that outlasts the probe's 3 s bound each read as unreachable (sh exit 1, ps1 unknown) within that bound, with no hang and no uncaught error. With MOE_DAEMON_HOST unset, or set to an IP literal or localhost, both launchers behave exactly as today.

scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs adds identity rows, on every engine the suite runs, where MOE_DAEMON_HOST is a DNS name that resolves to a fake /health applying the daemon's real isAllowedHealthHost. A daemon serving another project is refused with MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT, and this project's daemon is adopted. RED first: the name rows fail against the unchanged launchers, and the completion evidence quotes the failing output. All existing rows pass unchanged.

Verification runs in the task's own worktree or a git-archive snapshot, never with a build in the shared checkout. Command: `node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`, which exits 0. The evidence shows the PowerShell rows ran (not skipped) on at least one PowerShell engine.
taskRails: Do not loosen or bypass the daemon's /health Host guard (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/healthHost.ts). The launchers dial an IP literal instead, and healthHost.ts stays byte-identical.

implementationPlan.description:
Write the tests first, in scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs only. Read mem:gotcha-launcher-daemon-identity-probe and mem:gotcha-daemon-health-host-tests before you start. Every harness change below is backward compatible: every existing row and every existing assertion stays exactly as it is. (a) spawnAsync(exe, args, env = ENV), and runCheck(..., { daemonHost }) spawns with { ...ENV, MOE_DAEMON_HOST: daemonHost } when one is given. ENV still deletes the operator's own MOE_DAEMON_HOST. (b) listen(server, address = '127.0.0.1') and withHealth(statusCode, body, fn, { address = '127.0.0.1', guard = false } = {}). A guarded fake applies the daemon's REAL isAllowedHealthHost(req.headers.host, req.socket.localAddress). Import it lazily from packages/moe-daemon/dist/server/healthHost.js; that module imports only 'net'. If the dist is missing, fail the row with distKeys' 'build packages/moe-daemon first' wording. Never fall back to an unguarded fake. A refused Host gets 403 text/plain 'Forbidden', as the daemon does. Guarded requests are recorded as `${req.method} ${req.url} ${req.headers.host} ${code}`; unguarded recording stays 'GET /health'. (c) refusal() and assertRefused() take host = '127.0.0.1' as their last parameter. (d) powershellKeys' end anchor becomes the host-neutral '\n# Which project the daemon '. It matches the ps1 comment both today and after step 3 rewords it. (e) Resolve NAMES once, at load: 'localhost.' and os.hostname(). 'localhost.' is RFC 6761's localhost name in absolute form: every resolver answers loopback, yet it is not 'localhost', so a launcher must resolve it, and the guard 403s it as a Host. For each name, take the first entry of dns.promises.lookup(name, { all: true }). Node's default verbatim order is the OS getaddrinfo order that Python and .NET also use. Measured on this host: ::1 first for 'localhost.' on node, node.exe, python3, python.exe, PS 5.1 and PS 7. Skip the name's rows, with the reason, when: - the lookup fails; - the name is an IP literal or localhost; - the first address is IPv6 link-local (fe80::/10), because no Host can name a scoped address (on this Windows host os.hostname() resolves first to fe80::...%3); - a bind probe on the first address fails (no IPv6 loopback). The expected Host literal is [addr] for IPv6. Rows for each usable name, on every engine. The fake is guarded and listens on that first address. One admitted request means requests deep-equals [`GET /health ${literal}:${port} 200`]. - sh, live-pid branch (pidInfo). Foreign: assertRefused(..., name) plus one admitted request. Same: the running line plus one admitted request. - sh, Windows-owned candidate loop (px4Info; foreignSkip under Git Bash). Foreign: refused naming the name, r.after === r.before, '@@ exit host=[]', one admitted request. Same: adopted, '@@ exit host=[]' (the candidate is exported as given, never as the IP), one admitted request. - ps1, live-pid branch (psInfo). Foreign: refused naming `${name}:${port}`, untouched, no '@@ running=', one admitted request. Same: `@@ running=True port=${port} err=` plus one admitted request. Add one non-resolving-name guard row per engine on the live-pid branch: MOE_DAEMON_HOST='moe-daemon.invalid' (RFC 6761 .invalid never resolves) with closedPort(). It must be adopted exactly as today: sh 'running=true'; ps1 '@@ running=True port=

err=' with nothing after err=, which proves no exception reached $Error. These guard rows pass before and after the fix. RED: with both launchers untouched, run the step-4 checkRef. To iterate faster, keep its /mnt/d snapshot and re-run `node --test ...` and `node.exe --test ...` there after copying files in; the Linux leg fails first and stops the && chain, so get the PowerShell RED from node.exe directly. Every resolving-name row must fail. For sh, the guard 403s Host ':', the probe exits 1, and the row is adopted or unreachable. For ps1, it dials 127.0.0.1 and the fake sees zero requests. All existing rows and the guard rows must pass. Save the failing row names and diffs for the completion summary.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix scripts/moe-agent.sh, in probe_daemon_health only. It mirrors moe-proxy probeDaemonIdentity from task-86d66093.
Add ipaddress and socket to the python import line. Resolve inside the OUTER try:, right before the urlopen. Never put this code between comparable() and 'try:': the test's pythonKeys cuts from 'WINDOWS = re.compile(' to '\ntry:' and runs that cut with no argv. The python runs inside bash single quotes, so use double quotes only. The prototype below was verified on 2026-11-02 against the real guard. Old: Host 'localhost.:p' got 403 and exit 1. New: Host '[::1]:p' got 200 and exit 3 or 0. 127.0.0.1, [::1], LOCALHOST and bare ::1 still send exactly the Host they send today:
    host = sys.argv[1]
    try:
        ipaddress.ip_address(host[1:-1] if host[:1] == "[" and host[-1:] == "]" else host)
    except ValueError:
        if host.lower() != "localhost":
            address = socket.getaddrinfo(host, None, 0, socket.SOCK_STREAM)[0][4][0]
            host = "[%s]" % address if ":" in address else address
Then build the URL from host instead of sys.argv[1].
Error handling: a failed lookup raises inside the outer try, so the existing except Exception exits 1 (unreachable). A hung lookup is ended by the existing 3 s watchdog (os._exit(1)), which starts before it. Add no timer, no retry and no second address. IP literals and localhost (any case) keep the URL built from argv, byte for byte.
Leave comparable() untouched; it is task-3def0804's code. Also leave both call sites, refuse_foreign_daemon and the candidate loop untouched. The live-pid PROBE_HOST and the loop already pass the host as given, the loop still exports $CANDIDATE, and the refusal names '$1:$2', which is the name. Update the function's header comment in one or two lines: a name is resolved once and its first address dialed, because the daemon's /health guard 403s a name. `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` must pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix scripts/moe-agent.ps1. Keep its UTF-8 BOM, and never touch Get-MoeComparableProjectPath. The new signature is Get-MoeDaemonIdentity($Port, [string]$ProjectPath, [string]$ProbeHost = '127.0.0.1'). Never name the parameter $Host: it is PowerShell's read-only automatic variable. Before connecting, inside the existing try and the existing $deadline: - localhost in any ASCII case ($ProbeHost.ToLowerInvariant() -ceq 'localhost'; -eq is culture-aware, see mem:gotcha-powershell-path-comparison-culture) uses [Net.IPAddress]::Loopback. That is ps1's request today: Host 127.0.0.1:. - An IP literal (strip one pair of enclosing brackets, then [Net.IPAddress]::TryParse) uses that address, with no lookup. - Anything else gets one [Net.Dns]::GetHostAddressesAsync($ProbeHost), waited with [Threading.Tasks.Task]::WaitAny on the time left to $deadline. Return 'unknown' unless the task finished RanToCompletion with at least one address; otherwise use Result[0]. Then connect: New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient($address.AddressFamily). The PS 5.1 default TcpClient is IPv4-only and cannot reach ::1. Call ConnectAsync($address, [int]$Port) and wait on the time left, returning 'unknown' when none is left. The request line is "Host: ${hostText}:$([int]$Port)", where hostText is '[addr]' for InterNetworkV6 and the address otherwise. Keep the braces: "$hostText:" is a parse error. For 127.0.0.1 the request is byte-identical to today's. The rest of the function is unchanged: the read loop, the status check, the JSON, the comparison and 'foreign '. Error handling: never read .Result before checking Status. A faulted task's exception lands in $Error, and the harness's err= rows would show it. Every failure stays 'unknown' through the existing catch. Add no new throw. The call site is inside `if ($proc) {`, which the test cuts out together with the check block, so do not hoist it: $probeHost = if ($env:MOE_DAEMON_HOST) { $env:MOE_DAEMON_HOST } else { '127.0.0.1' }. Pass $probeHost as the third argument. The refusal's first line reads 'the daemon at ${probeHost}:$($info.port)'. The three sentences are otherwise byte-identical (REFUSAL_FIXED), matching sh's '$1:$2'. Reword the comment above the function so it names the probed host and the resolve rule; keep its first words '# Which project the daemon ' for the test anchor. Prototype, verified on 2026-11-02 on PS 5.1 and PS 7 against the real guard: - 'localhost.' sent Host [::1]:

and classified foreign and same correctly. - 127.0.0.1, LOCALHOST and [::1] sent today's Host. - 'moe-daemon.invalid' gave 'unknown' in under 0.1 s, with $Error empty.
implementationPlan.note: Added ProbeHost default, literal/localhost handling, async DNS once with Status-before-Result and deadline-bound WaitAny, address-family TcpClient, literal Host (IPv6 brackets), and env-aware call/refusal. BOM EF BB BF preserved; Get-MoeComparableProjectPath and remaining HTTP/parser logic untouched. Minor same-scope plan correction: use ToLowerInvariant().Equals('localhost') (ordinal) instead of -ceq. Fresh PS5.1 probe proved ('local'+[char]173+'host') -ceq 'localhost' is True but ordinal Equals is False; -ceq remains culture-aware and would bypass resolution for non-localhost names (as preloaded culture memory warns). Gate batched to step 4.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When MOE_DAEMON_HOST is a DNS name (neither an IP literal nor localhost in any case), both launchers' pre-flight /health identity probes resolve it once. They dial its first address in OS order and send that IP literal as the Host, bracketed for IPv6; the daemon's /health guard admits it. A daemon at that name serving another project is refused with MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT, naming the configured host and port. This project's daemon is adopted, and the sh candidate loop still exports the candidate as given. moe-agent.ps1 now probes MOE_DAEMON_HOST when it is set, else 127.0.0.1. IP literals, localhost and an unset MOE_DAEMON_HOST keep today's requests. A failed or hung lookup reads as unreachable (sh exit 1, ps1 'unknown') inside the existing 3 s bound.
acceptanceCriteria: sh probe_daemon_health given a name sends one GET /health whose Host is '<ip literal>:<port>', bracketed for IPv6. A foreign project gives exit 3 and a refusal naming '<name>:<port>'; this project gives exit 0. The candidate loop exports the name, never the resolved IP.
ps1 probes $env:MOE_DAEMON_HOST, else 127.0.0.1. A name is handled as in sh. The refusal's first line names '<probe host>:<port>', and the other two lines are unchanged.
With an IP literal, localhost or an unset MOE_DAEMON_HOST, the request bytes are unchanged: sh builds the URL from argv, and ps1 sends Host 127.0.0.1:<port> for unset and for localhost.
A failed lookup gives sh exit 1 and ps1 'unknown' with $Error untouched. A hung lookup gives the same result within 3 s, through the sh watchdog and the ps1 WaitAny on the deadline.

'localhost.' rows (plus os.hostname() where usable) run on every engine against a fake guarded by the real isAllowedHealthHost: a foreign project is refused and this project adopted. RED is shown on the unchanged launchers, and every existing row passes unchanged.

Probe time stays at most 3 s in total: one watchdog in sh, one deadline in ps1, and no extra timers.
The probe never throws: sh exits only 0, 1 or 3; ps1 returns only 'same', 'foreign <path>' or 'unknown'.
moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM. No added line contains a project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected approaches:
- Admitting names, or the configured host, in healthHost.ts. The task rail forbids it, and anyone who controls that name's DNS could then rebind it.
- Dialing the name but sending a forged 'Host: 127.0.0.1'. The guard admits any 127/8 Host, so it would work, but it sidesteps the rebinding rule, and the rail says to dial an IP literal.
- Trying every resolved address. The DoD and the proxy both take the first one: one bounded attempt.
- ps1 dialing 'localhost' by name. PS 7's dual-mode TcpClient tries ::1 first, and on Windows a refused loopback connect costs about 2.4 s of the 3 s budget. So localhost keeps ps1's 127.0.0.1 request, which is also today's request (DoD 3).
- os.hostname() as the only test name. On this Windows host it resolves first to a scoped link-local fe80::...%3, so every PowerShell row would skip and DoD 5 could not be shown.
Chosen instead: 'localhost.' (RFC 6761). It resolves to ::1 first on every engine, the guard still refuses it as a name, and it exercises the IPv6-bracket path. os.hostname() stays as the IPv4 case wherever it is usable (127.0.1.1 in WSL).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Prototypes of both fixes, in scratch only, were run against a fake applying the real dist isAllowedHealthHost.
sh: old code sent Host 'localhost.:p' and got 403, exit 1. New code sends Host '[::1]:p' and gets exit 3 for foreign, 0 for same. 127.0.0.1, [::1], LOCALHOST and bare ::1 send the same Host as before.
ps1 (PS 5.1 and 7): 'localhost.' gives foreign or same via [::1]. 127.0.0.1 and LOCALHOST send Host 127.0.0.1. A failed lookup gives unknown with $Error empty.
Harness facts:
- pythonKeys runs the WINDOWS..try: cut without argv, so the new python goes inside try:.
- SEGMENTS.ps1.check cuts from the Test-Path block to `if (-not $running)`, so $probeHost must live inside it.
- The harness prints err=$Error[0].
- runCheck already returns before/after (task-3def0804, landed 7beed0bc).
The gate dry run exited 0 in about 5 min.
planningNotes.risks:
- Engines must pick Node's first address, or the fake is on the wrong one. Verified on this host for 'localhost.'. CI Linux engines share glibc. A host without IPv6 loopback skips those rows through the bind probe.
- PowerShell traps: $Host is read-only; "$var:" is a parse error; reading .Result of a faulted task pollutes $Error; the PS 5.1 default TcpClient is IPv4-only.
- The ps1 RED needs the Windows leg (node.exe). The unchanged ps1 connects to a closed 127.0.0.1 port, which takes about 2.4 s on Windows: slow, not hung.
- Residuals, out of scope: a bare IPv6 MOE_DAEMON_HOST on sh, a scoped link-local first address, and trying only the first address. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:512 now asks more of clients than ours need, but it is not one of this task's lane files.
- isEpicFinal is only the order fallback of a long-running bucket epic. The gate is the DoD's full launcher-identity suite on every engine, not a whole-epic sweep. The qualityGate (parity plus npm run lint) still runs at landing.
- The WORKING claim waits for task-3def0804, which is in REVIEW.
